modules.title: Using an Automated External Defibrillator (AED)
modules.description: An AED is a portable device that can analyze heart rhythm and deliver a shock to restore a normal rhythm during sudden cardiac arrest, and modern AEDs are designed to guide untrained bystanders through use. This lesson covers safe, correct AED operation alongside CPR.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Using an Automated External Defibrillator (AED)

An AED is a portable device that can analyze heart rhythm and deliver a shock to restore a normal rhythm during sudden cardiac arrest, and modern AEDs are designed to guide untrained bystanders through use.
steps: Turn on the AED and follow its voice prompts exactly
Attach the pads to the person's bare, dry chest as shown in the diagrams on the pads
Ensure no one is touching the person while the AED analyzes the heart rhythm
If a shock is advised, ensure everyone is clear, then press the shock button, and resume CPR immediately after
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Using an Automated External Defibrillator (AED)" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What must you do before an AED delivers a shock, and immediately after?
quiz.a: Ensure no one is touching the person before the shock, and resume CPR immediately after the shock is delivered

modules.pro_tip: Continue CPR between AED prompts; the device will re-analyze the rhythm periodically and tell you when to stop.

modules.title: Recovery Position for an Unresponsive Breathing Person
modules.description: The recovery position keeps an unresponsive but breathing person's airway clear and allows fluids to drain from the mouth, preventing choking, while awaiting emergency help. This lesson covers the step-by-step positioning technique.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Recovery Position for an Unresponsive Breathing Person
The recovery position keeps an unresponsive but breathing person's airway clear and allows fluids to drain from the mouth, preventing choking, while awaiting emergency help.
steps: Kneel beside the person and place the arm nearest you at a right angle to their body
Bring their far arm across their chest and hold the back of their hand against their near cheek
Grab the far knee and pull it up, rolling the person toward you onto their side
Tilt the head back slightly to keep the airway open and check breathing regularly until help arrives
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Recovery Position for an Unresponsive Breathing Person" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why is the recovery position used for an unresponsive but breathing person?
quiz.a: It keeps the airway open and lets vomit or fluid drain out of the mouth instead of causing choking

modules.pro_tip: Never place an unresponsive breathing person flat on their back unattended; always use the recovery position.

modules.title: Recognizing a Heart Attack
modules.description: A heart attack occurs when blood flow to part of the heart is blocked, and recognizing symptoms quickly and acting fast dramatically improves outcomes. This lesson covers common warning signs, which can differ between men and women.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Recognizing a Heart Attack
A heart attack occurs when blood flow to part of the heart is blocked, and recognizing symptoms quickly and acting fast dramatically improves outcomes.
steps: Watch for chest pain or pressure, often described as squeezing or heavy, lasting more than a few minutes
Note other signs: pain radiating to the arm, jaw, or back, shortness of breath, nausea, or cold sweat
Call emergency services immediately; do not attempt to drive the person yourself
If not allergic and advised by dispatch, have the person chew an aspirin while waiting for help
materials_needed: Aspirin, if available and not contraindicated
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Recognizing a Heart Attack" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What is a classic symptom of a heart attack besides chest pain?

modules.title: Responding to an Allergic Reaction and Epinephrine Auto-Injector Use
modules.description: Severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) can rapidly become life-threatening, causing airway swelling and blood pressure drops, and require immediate epinephrine administration if available. This lesson covers recognizing anaphylaxis and using an EpiPen-style auto-injector.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Responding to an Allergic Reaction and Epinephrine Auto-Injector Use
Severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) can rapidly become life-threatening, causing airway swelling and blood pressure drops, and require immediate epinephrine administration if available.
steps: Recognize signs of anaphylaxis: hives, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness

Remove the safety cap and firmly press the injector against the outer mid-thigh until it clicks, holding for several seconds

quiz.q: Where on the body is an epinephrine auto-injector typically administered?

modules.pro_tip: Always call emergency services after using an EpiPen, even if the person seems to improve, since symptoms can return.

modules.title: Recognizing and Treating Heat Exhaustion and Heat Stroke

Heat exhaustion and heat stroke exist on a spectrum of heat-related illness, with heat stroke being a life-threatening emergency requiring rapid cooling.
steps: For heat exhaustion (heavy sweating, weakness, nausea): move to shade, remove excess clothing, sip water, and cool with a wet cloth

modules.title: Recognizing and Treating Hypothermia
modules.description: Hypothermia occurs when the body loses heat faster than it can produce it, dropping core temperature to dangerous levels, and can occur even in mild, wet, and windy conditions, not just extreme cold. This lesson covers warning signs and safe rewarming.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Recognizing and Treating Hypothermia
Hypothermia occurs when the body loses heat faster than it can produce it, dropping core temperature to dangerous levels, and can occur even in mild, wet, and windy conditions, not just extreme cold.
steps: Watch for signs: shivering, confusion, slurred speech, drowsiness, and fumbling hands
Move the person to a warm, dry location and remove any wet clothing
Wrap them in warm, dry blankets, focusing on the torso, and cover the head
Give warm (not hot) sweet drinks if they're fully alert; never give alcohol or rub their limbs vigorously
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Recognizing and Treating Hypothermia" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why shouldn't you vigorously rub or massage a hypothermic person's limbs?
quiz.a: It can push cold blood from the extremities back to the heart too quickly, risking dangerous heart rhythm problems

modules.pro_tip: Warm the core of the body (torso) first rather than the extremities to rewarm safely.

modules.title: Treating Eye Injuries
modules.description: Eye injuries require careful, gentle first aid since the eye is delicate and improper handling can worsen damage. This lesson covers flushing chemical exposure and handling embedded objects safely.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Treating Eye Injuries
Eye injuries require careful, gentle first aid since the eye is delicate and improper handling can worsen damage.
steps: For chemical exposure, flush the eye continuously with clean water for at least 15-20 minutes
For a foreign object on the surface, try gently flushing it out with water; do not rub the eye
If an object is embedded in the eye, do not attempt to remove it; stabilize it and cover both eyes loosely
Seek emergency medical care for any significant eye injury, even if it initially seems minor
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Treating Eye Injuries" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What should you do if an object is embedded in someone's eye?

modules.title: Managing Dental Injuries (Knocked-Out Tooth)
modules.description: A knocked-out permanent tooth can often be saved if handled and reinserted or preserved correctly within a short window of time. This lesson covers proper handling and storage of an avulsed tooth.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Managing Dental Injuries (Knocked-Out Tooth)
A knocked-out permanent tooth can often be saved if handled and reinserted or preserved correctly within a short window of time.
steps: Pick the tooth up by the crown (chewing surface), never touching the root
Rinse it gently with milk or saline if dirty, without scrubbing
If possible, try to reinsert it gently into the socket and have the person bite down on gauze to hold it
If reinsertion isn't possible, store the tooth in milk and seek a dentist immediately, ideally within 30-60 minutes
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Managing Dental Injuries (Knocked-Out Tooth)" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid touching the root of a knocked-out tooth?
quiz.a: The root contains delicate cells needed for reattachment, which can be damaged by handling or drying out

modules.pro_tip: Store an avulsed tooth in milk, not water, since milk's pH and composition better preserve the root cells.

modules.title: Assembling a Workplace First Aid Kit
modules.description: Workplace first aid kits often need to meet specific regulatory standards and account for job-specific hazards, differing from a basic home kit. This lesson covers workplace-specific considerations and regular maintenance responsibilities.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Assembling a Workplace First Aid Kit
Workplace first aid kits often need to meet specific regulatory standards and account for job-specific hazards, differing from a basic home kit.
steps: Assess job-specific risks, such as burns in a kitchen or cuts in a workshop, and stock accordingly
Designate and train specific staff members as first aiders
Post the kit's location clearly and keep it accessible to all employees, including any relevant safety regulations
Log incidents and restock supplies immediately after use, checking expiration dates regularly
materials_needed: Eyewash station or solution (for relevant workplaces)

modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Assembling a Workplace First Aid Kit" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why might a workplace first aid kit differ from a basic home kit?

modules.title: First Aid for Burns: Assessing Severity
modules.description: Burns are classified by depth (first, second, and third-degree) and this classification determines appropriate first aid and whether professional treatment is needed. This lesson builds on basic burn care by teaching how to assess severity.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: First Aid for Burns: Assessing Severity
Burns are classified by depth (first, second, and third-degree) and this classification determines appropriate first aid and whether professional treatment is needed.
steps: Identify a first-degree burn: red, painful, no blisters, affecting only the top skin layer
Identify a second-degree burn: blistering, intense pain, and a wet or shiny appearance
Identify a third-degree burn: white, leathery, or charred skin that may appear painless due to nerve damage
Cool any burn under running water for 20 minutes and seek emergency care for large, deep, or third-degree burns
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "First Aid for Burns: Assessing Severity" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why might a severe third-degree burn feel less painful than a milder burn?
quiz.a: Third-degree burns destroy nerve endings in the skin, which can reduce or eliminate pain sensation at the burn site

modules.pro_tip: Never apply ice, butter, or ointments to a burn; cool running water is the safest first response.

modules.title: Managing Asthma Attacks and Breathing Emergencies
modules.description: Recognizing an asthma attack and helping someone use their rescue inhaler correctly can prevent a breathing emergency from becoming life-threatening. This lesson covers inhaler assistance and when to escalate to emergency care.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Managing Asthma Attacks and Breathing Emergencies
Recognizing an asthma attack and helping someone use their rescue inhaler correctly can prevent a breathing emergency from becoming life-threatening.
steps: Help the person sit upright, not lying down, and stay calm to reduce panic

modules.title: Diabetic Emergencies: Low and High Blood Sugar
modules.description: Diabetic emergencies can involve dangerously low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) or high blood sugar (hyperglycemia), which look different and require different responses. This lesson covers recognizing and responding to both.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Diabetic Emergencies: Low and High Blood Sugar
Diabetic emergencies can involve dangerously low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) or high blood sugar (hyperglycemia), which look different and require different responses.
steps: Recognize low blood sugar: sudden confusion, shakiness, sweating, and irritability

Recognize high blood sugar: excessive thirst, frequent urination, and fruity-smelling breath, developing more slowly

modules.title: Spinal Injury Precautions
modules.description: A suspected spinal injury requires careful handling to avoid worsening potential nerve damage, and in most cases the person should not be moved unless in immediate danger. This lesson covers recognizing red flags and safe head stabilization.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Spinal Injury Precautions
A suspected spinal injury requires careful handling to avoid worsening potential nerve damage, and in most cases the person should not be moved unless in immediate danger.
steps: Suspect a spinal injury after falls, vehicle accidents, or diving incidents, especially with neck or back pain, numbness, or weakness
Tell the person to stay completely still and avoid moving their head or neck
Stabilize their head in the position found by placing hands on either side, without pulling or twisting
Only move the person if they are in immediate danger, such as fire, using the safest method available

Research on skill acquisition consistently shows that people learn physical and procedural skills best in three phases: first understanding what correct execution looks like, then practising slowly with full attention to form, and finally adding speed, pressure, or complexity only after the basic pattern is stable. modules.title: Treating Frostbite
modules.description: Frostbite is the freezing of skin and underlying tissue, most common on fingers, toes, ears, and nose, and requires gentle, gradual rewarming rather than rubbing or direct heat. This lesson covers recognition and safe field treatment.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Treating Frostbite
Frostbite is the freezing of skin and underlying tissue, most common on fingers, toes, ears, and nose, and requires gentle, gradual rewarming rather than rubbing or direct heat.
steps: Recognize frostbite: numbness, waxy or pale skin, and hardness to the touch in affected areas
Move to a warm environment and remove any wet or constricting clothing and jewelry
Rewarm the area gradually in warm (not hot) water around 37-40C (98-104F), never using direct heat like a fire
Do not rub or massage the frostbitten area, and seek medical care, especially if blistering or severe numbness occurs
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Treating Frostbite" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why should a frostbitten area never be rubbed or massaged?
quiz.a: Ice crystals in the frozen tissue can cause further damage to skin and blood vessels if rubbed

modules.pro_tip: Never rewarm a frostbitten area if there's a chance it could refreeze before reaching definitive care, since refreezing causes worse damage.

modules.title: Heat-Related Cramps and Prevention
modules.description: Heat cramps are painful muscle spasms caused by heavy sweating and electrolyte loss during exertion in heat, often an early warning sign before more serious heat illness develops. This lesson covers treatment and prevention strategies.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Heat-Related Cramps and Prevention
Heat cramps are painful muscle spasms caused by heavy sweating and electrolyte loss during exertion in heat, often an early warning sign before more serious heat illness develops.
steps: Move the person to a cool, shaded area and stop physical activity
Gently stretch and massage the cramping muscle
Give water or an electrolyte drink, avoiding alcohol or caffeine
Watch for progression to heat exhaustion, and rest for several hours before resuming activity
materials_needed: Water or a sports drink with electrolytes
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Heat-Related Cramps and Prevention" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why can heat cramps be an early warning sign of a more serious condition?
quiz.a: They indicate the body is already struggling with fluid and electrolyte loss, which can progress to heat exhaustion or heat stroke if ignored

modules.pro_tip: Rest and rehydrate fully after heat cramps rather than pushing through, since continuing can lead to more serious heat illness.

modules.title: Basic Wilderness First Aid Principles
modules.description: Wilderness first aid differs from urban first aid because professional help may be hours or days away, requiring more improvisation and sustained care. This lesson introduces the key mindset shifts for remote settings.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Basic Wilderness First Aid Principles
Wilderness first aid differs from urban first aid because professional help may be hours or days away, requiring more improvisation and sustained care.
steps: Assess the scene for ongoing danger before approaching, since remote hazards like terrain or wildlife may persist
Prioritize preventing further injury and stabilizing the person for what may be a long wait for help
Use improvised materials, like trekking poles or clothing, for splints and bandages when supplies are limited
Plan for evacuation: decide whether to signal for help, send someone for help, or move the person yourself
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Basic Wilderness First Aid Principles" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: How does wilderness first aid differ from city first aid in terms of priorities?
quiz.a: Since professional help can be hours or days away, wilderness first aid focuses more on sustained stabilization and improvisation with limited supplies

modules.pro_tip: Always tell someone your planned route and return time before heading into the wilderness, so help can be sent if you don't return.

modules.title: Signaling for Help in Remote Areas
modules.description: When lost or injured far from help, knowing how to signal effectively increases the chances of being found quickly. This lesson covers universal distress signals and tools for attracting attention.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Signaling for Help in Remote Areas
When lost or injured far from help, knowing how to signal effectively increases the chances of being found quickly.
steps: Use three of anything (three whistle blasts, three fires, three shouts) as the universal distress signal
Use a signal mirror to flash sunlight toward aircraft or distant searchers
Lay out brightly colored clothing or gear in an open area to be visible from above
Stay in one place once you've signaled, since moving makes you harder to relocate
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Signaling for Help in Remote Areas" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What does the pattern of 'three' signify in wilderness distress signaling?
quiz.a: Three of any signal (blasts, flashes, shouts, fires) is the internationally recognized distress signal

modules.pro_tip: Once you've begun signaling, stay put in an open, visible area so searchers can find you rather than chasing a moving target.

modules.title: Managing Anaphylaxis Without an Auto-Injector

learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Managing Anaphylaxis Without an Auto-Injector

modules.title: Head Injury and Concussion Assessment
modules.description: Head injuries range from minor bumps to serious traumatic brain injuries, and recognizing warning signs helps determine when emergency care is needed. This lesson covers concussion symptoms and monitoring guidelines.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Head Injury and Concussion Assessment
Head injuries range from minor bumps to serious traumatic brain injuries, and recognizing warning signs helps determine when emergency care is needed.
steps: Watch for immediate symptoms: confusion, dizziness, headache, nausea, or brief loss of consciousness
Apply a cold compress to any swelling and have the person rest without strenuous activity
Monitor for worsening red-flag symptoms over the next 24-48 hours: repeated vomiting, worsening headache, or unequal pupils
Seek emergency care immediately if the person loses consciousness, has a seizure, or shows worsening confusion

quiz.q: Name two red-flag symptoms after a head injury that require immediate emergency care.
quiz.a: Any two of: loss of consciousness, repeated vomiting, seizure, unequal pupil size, or worsening confusion

modules.pro_tip: Someone with a possible concussion should not be left alone for the first 24 hours, and should avoid strenuous activity or screens until cleared by a doctor.

modules.title: Chest and Abdominal Injury First Aid
modules.description: Chest and abdominal injuries can be life-threatening internally even when the outside looks minor, so careful assessment and specific handling techniques matter. This lesson covers penetrating wounds and impaled objects.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Chest and Abdominal Injury First Aid
Chest and abdominal injuries can be life-threatening internally even when the outside looks minor, so careful assessment and specific handling techniques matter.
steps: For a penetrating chest wound, cover it with a dressing taped on three sides to allow air to escape but not enter
Watch closely for signs of worsening breathing difficulty, which may indicate a collapsed lung
For an impaled object in the abdomen or elsewhere, never remove it; stabilize it in place with bulky dressings around it
Call emergency services immediately for any penetrating chest or abdominal injury
materials_needed: Plastic wrap or occlusive dressing (for chest wounds)
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Chest and Abdominal Injury First Aid" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why is an impaled object left in place rather than removed?
quiz.a: The object may be plugging a wound and preventing severe bleeding; removing it can cause catastrophic blood loss

Chest and abdominal injuries can be life-threatening internally even when the outside looks minor, so careful assessment and specific handling techniques matter. This lesson covers penetrating wounds and impaled objects. In this lesson you will break the skill into learnable parts, practise each part slowly and deliberately, and then reassemble them into a smooth whole, which is how experienced practitioners in every field actually build their fluency.

Research on skill acquisition consistently shows that people learn physical and procedural skills best in three phases: first understanding what correct execution looks like, then practising slowly with full attention to form, and finally adding speed, pressure, or complexity only after the basic pattern is stable. This lesson is organised around exactly that progression, so resist the temptation to skip ahead -- the order is doing real work.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to: Understand and safely practice: Chest and Abdominal Injury First Aid; Chest and abdominal injuries can be life-threatening internally even when the outside looks minor, so careful assessment and specific handling techniques matter. Keep these objectives visible as you work -- they are the measuring stick for whether the practice is working, and each one is phrased as something you can actually demonstrate rather than something you vaguely feel familiar with. Vague familiarity is the great impostor of learning; demonstrable ability is the real thing.

Set up your workspace before beginning. The materials for this lesson are: Sterile dressings, Plastic wrap or occlusive dressing (for chest wounds). Beyond the physical items, prepare the situation too: give yourself enough uninterrupted time to work through the steps slowly at least twice, choose a space where you can concentrate, and if the skill benefits from supervision or a partner, arrange that in advance. Professionals in every hands-on field treat setup as part of the skill itself, not a chore before the skill -- adopting that mindset early will serve you in every lesson that follows.

Here is the step-by-step method. As you work through it, narrate each step to yourself in your own words -- explaining as you go is one of the most reliable ways to move a procedure from short-term memory into lasting skill. If this step feels awkward at first, that is normal; repeat it in isolation a few times until it smooths out before continuing. Step 2: Watch closely for signs of worsening breathing difficulty, which may indicate a collapsed lung. Pay particular attention here, because this is a step where small errors tend to compound later in the sequence. Step 3: For an impaled object in the abdomen or elsewhere, never remove it; stabilize it in place with bulky dressings around it. modules.title: Basic Triage Concepts
modules.description: Triage is the process of prioritizing care when there are multiple injured people and limited resources, ensuring the most critical patients are treated first. This lesson introduces the basic principles of triage used by first responders.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Basic Triage Concepts

modules.title: Moving and Transporting an Injured Person Safely
modules.description: Sometimes an injured person must be moved before help arrives, and doing so safely protects both the injured person and the helper from further harm. This lesson covers safe lifting and improvised carrying techniques.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Moving and Transporting an Injured Person Safely
Sometimes an injured person must be moved before help arrives, and doing so safely protects both the injured person and the helper from further harm.
steps: Only move someone if there's immediate danger or professional help can't reach them
Lift with your legs, not your back, keeping the injured person's body as aligned as possible
For a suspected spinal injury, use a coordinated log-roll technique with multiple helpers if movement is unavoidable
Use a sturdy blanket or tarp as an improvised stretcher when carrying someone any distance
materials_needed: Sturdy blanket or tarp (for improvised carrying)
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Moving and Transporting an Injured Person Safely" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why is a coordinated log-roll used when moving someone with a suspected spinal injury?
quiz.a: It keeps the spine aligned as a single unit during movement, minimizing the risk of further nerve damage

modules.pro_tip: Get as many helpers as possible before moving an injured person, since more hands means smoother, safer movement.

modules.title: Advanced Wound Packing for Severe Bleeding
modules.description: For deep wounds where direct pressure alone isn't enough, packing the wound with gauze helps apply pressure from within, a technique commonly taught in advanced trauma courses (like Stop the Bleed). This lesson covers safe wound packing technique.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Advanced Wound Packing for Severe Bleeding
For deep wounds where direct pressure alone isn't enough, packing the wound with gauze helps apply pressure from within, a technique commonly taught in advanced trauma courses (like Stop the Bleed).
steps: Put on gloves and locate the source of bleeding within the wound
Pack the gauze firmly and directly into the wound cavity, pressing it into contact with the bleeding source
Continue packing until the wound cavity is filled, then apply firm direct pressure on top
Hold pressure continuously for at least 3 minutes, then secure with a pressure bandage and seek emergency care
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Advanced Wound Packing for Severe Bleeding" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why is wound packing sometimes necessary instead of just surface pressure?
quiz.a: For deep wounds, surface pressure alone doesn't reach the bleeding source; packing fills the cavity to apply pressure where the bleeding originates

modules.pro_tip: Hemostatic gauze, which helps blood clot faster, is especially useful for severe wounds if available in an advanced kit.

modules.title: Applying and Using a Tourniquet Correctly
modules.description: A tourniquet is a life-saving device for severe limb bleeding that direct pressure cannot control, and modern trauma guidelines encourage its use much earlier than older first aid teaching suggested. This lesson covers correct tourniquet placement and timing.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Applying and Using a Tourniquet Correctly
A tourniquet is a life-saving device for severe limb bleeding that direct pressure cannot control, and modern trauma guidelines encourage its use much earlier than older first aid teaching suggested.
steps: Place the tourniquet 5-7cm above the wound, avoiding joints, never directly on the wound itself
Tighten it until bleeding stops completely, which will be significantly tighter and more painful than expected
Note and write down the exact time the tourniquet was applied, ideally on the tourniquet itself or the person's skin
Do not loosen or remove the tourniquet once applied; leave that decision to medical professionals
materials_needed: Commercial tourniquet (or improvised wide, flat material)
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Applying and Using a Tourniquet Correctly" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Where should a tourniquet be placed relative to a bleeding wound?
quiz.a: About 5-7cm above the wound, avoiding joints, high enough on the limb, never directly over the wound

modules.pro_tip: Write the application time directly on the tourniquet or the patient's forehead, since this critically informs medical treatment.

modules.title: Multi-Casualty and Disaster Preparedness Basics
modules.description: In disasters or mass-casualty events, first aid priorities shift toward triage, resourcefulness, and coordination since normal emergency response may be delayed or overwhelmed. This lesson introduces core preparedness concepts for such scenarios.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Multi-Casualty and Disaster Preparedness Basics
In disasters or mass-casualty events, first aid priorities shift toward triage, resourcefulness, and coordination since normal emergency response may be delayed or overwhelmed.
steps: Prepare an emergency kit in advance with supplies for at least 72 hours

modules.title: Long-Term Wound Monitoring and Infection Signs
modules.description: Even properly treated wounds can become infected days later, so knowing what to monitor for after initial first aid is an important extended-care skill. This lesson covers signs of infection and when to seek follow-up care.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Long-Term Wound Monitoring and Infection Signs
Even properly treated wounds can become infected days later, so knowing what to monitor for after initial first aid is an important extended-care skill.
steps: Change dressings regularly and inspect the wound each time for changes
Watch for infection signs: increasing redness, warmth, swelling, pus, or worsening pain after the first day or two

Seek medical care promptly if red streaking spreads from the wound, which can indicate a spreading infection
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Long-Term Wound Monitoring and Infection Signs" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What does red streaking spreading away from a wound typically indicate?

modules.pro_tip: Take a photo of a wound each day when changing the dressing, which makes it easier to notice gradual changes.

modules.title: Assisting Childbirth in an Emergency
modules.description: While rare, being prepared for an unplanned emergency delivery when professional help isn't immediately available is a valuable advanced first aid skill. This lesson covers the basics of supporting a safe, calm emergency birth.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Assisting Childbirth in an Emergency
While rare, being prepared for an unplanned emergency delivery when professional help isn't immediately available is a valuable advanced first aid skill.
steps: Call emergency services immediately and stay on the line for guided instructions if possible
Help the mother into a comfortable position and reassure her; do not try to delay or hold back delivery
Support the baby's head and shoulders gently as it emerges, without pulling
Once born, dry and wrap the baby immediately to keep warm, and keep both mother and baby calm until help arrives
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Assisting Childbirth in an Emergency" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What is the first and most important action if you find yourself assisting an unplanned emergency birth?

modules.pro_tip: Never try to hold a baby back from being delivered or pull it out forcefully; let the process happen naturally while you support and guide.

modules.title: Mental Health First Aid and Crisis Support
modules.description: Mental health emergencies, including panic attacks and suicidal crises, require calm, non-judgmental first aid just as physical emergencies do. This lesson introduces basic mental health first aid principles and crisis resources.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Mental Health First Aid and Crisis Support
Mental health emergencies, including panic attacks and suicidal crises, require calm, non-judgmental first aid just as physical emergencies do.
steps: Stay calm, listen without judgment, and avoid minimizing what the person is feeling
For a panic attack, guide slow breathing and reassure them that it will pass, usually within 20-30 minutes
If someone expresses thoughts of self-harm, ask directly and calmly whether they're thinking of hurting themselves
Connect them to professional help, such as a crisis line or emergency services, and don't leave them alone if risk seems immediate
materials_needed: Crisis hotline number saved in phone
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Mental Health First Aid and Crisis Support" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why is directly asking someone about suicidal thoughts recommended rather than avoided?
quiz.a: Research shows asking directly does not increase risk and can open the door for the person to get help; avoiding it can leave them isolated

modules.pro_tip: Keep a mental health crisis line number saved in your phone in advance, just like any other emergency contact.

skills.title: Identify Coins and Notes
skills.description: Learn to identify different coins and notes by their values. Practise counting change. Understand that money is exchanged for goods and services.

skills.title: Save vs Spend
skills.description: Use three jars: Save, Spend, Give. When you receive money, divide it between the jars. The 'Save' jar is for bigger goals.

quiz.question: If you have £1 and spend 40p, how much do you have left?
What is the best habit when you receive money?

skills.title: Budget Your Pocket Money
skills.description: List income (pocket money, gifts). List planned expenses. Subtract expenses from income. If negative, reduce spending. Track actual spending for one month.
skills.why: Budgeting prevents debt and teaches priorities.

skills.title: Needs vs Wants
skills.description: Needs are essentials (food, shelter, clothing). Wants are nice-to-haves (games, sweets, toys). Before buying, ask: 'Is this a need or a want?'
skills.why: Distinguishing needs and wants prevents impulsive spending.

quiz.question: Which of these is a NEED?
If your income is £20 and expenses are £25, what should you do?

skills.title: Understand Compound Interest
skills.description: Compound interest means interest is earned on both the original amount AND previous interest. £100 at 5% per year: Year 1 = £105, Year 2 = £110.25, Year 3 = £115.76. The longer you save, the faster it grows.
skills.why: Understanding compound interest makes you a smarter saver and borrower.

skills.title: Taxes: What and Why
skills.description: Tax is money collected by governments to fund public services (schools, hospitals, roads). Income tax is paid on earnings. VAT is added to goods. Understanding tax helps you plan your finances as an adult.
skills.why: Every citizen needs to understand tax to participate in the economy.

quiz.question: If you invest £1000 at 10% compound interest, what do you have after 2 years?

skills.title: What is Money?
skills.explanation: Understand the purpose and forms of money.
steps: Money is a medium of exchange used to buy goods and services.
Money comes in coins, notes, and digital forms.
Barter (swapping goods directly) existed before money.
Different countries use different currencies.
The value of money can change over time (inflation).
skills.tip: Keep your money safe — only share payment details with trusted adults.

quiz.question: What is a currency?
options: The money used in a country

skills.title: Earning Money
steps: Income is money earned from working.
Wages are paid per hour; salary is a fixed annual amount.
Businesses earn money by selling products or services.
Tax is taken from income to fund public services.
Freelancers are self-employed workers.
skills.tip: Track your pocket money or earnings in a notebook to understand income.

quiz.question: What is income tax used for?

skills.title: Budgeting
skills.explanation: Plan spending to stay within your income.
steps: List all income (money coming in).
List all essential expenses: rent, food, transport.
List optional spending: entertainment, eating out.
Subtract expenses from income to find remaining money.
Adjust spending so you do not spend more than you earn.

quiz.question: A budget is?
options: A plan for how to spend and save money

skills.title: Saving and Interest
skills.explanation: Understand why and how to save money.
steps: Saving means keeping money for future use.
A savings account in a bank earns interest.
Interest is a percentage added to your savings over time.
Compound interest earns interest on interest — money grows faster.
Set a savings goal to stay motivated.
skills.tip: Start saving early — even small amounts grow with compound interest.

quiz.question: Compound interest means?
options: Interest only on the original amount
Interest on both the original amount and previous interest

skills.title: Smart Spending
steps: Distinguish between needs (essentials) and wants (luxuries).
Compare prices before buying — look for value, not just cheapness.
Avoid impulse buying: wait 24 hours before purchasing.
Check return policies before buying.
Use lists when shopping to avoid overspending.
skills.tip: Advertising is designed to make you want things — be a critical consumer.

quiz.question: A 'need' is?
options: Something essential like food or shelter

quiz.question: Best way to avoid impulse buying?

modules.title: Building an Emergency Fund

modules.title: How Compound Interest Works
modules.description: Compound interest is interest calculated on both the original amount and previously earned interest, causing savings or debt to grow exponentially over time rather than linearly. This lesson demonstrates the powerful effect of starting to save early.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: How Compound Interest Works
Compound interest is interest calculated on both the original amount and previously earned interest, causing savings or debt to grow exponentially over time rather than linearly.
steps: Understand that compound interest earns 'interest on interest,' unlike simple interest
Calculate how a small amount grows over many years using a compound interest formula or calculator
Compare how starting to save 10 years earlier can result in far more money despite contributing less overall
Recognize that compound interest works against you with debt just as it works for you with savings
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "How Compound Interest Works" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why can someone who starts saving 10 years earlier end up with more money than someone who saves more per month but starts later?

modules.pro_tip: The single biggest lever in compound growth is time, so starting early matters more than the amount you start with.

modules.title: Understanding Credit Scores
modules.description: A credit score is a numeric representation of creditworthiness, typically ranging from 300-850, that lenders use to decide whether to extend credit and at what interest rate. This lesson covers what factors make up a credit score and why it matters.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Understanding Credit Scores
A credit score is a numeric representation of creditworthiness, typically ranging from 300-850, that lenders use to decide whether to extend credit and at what interest rate.
steps: Understand the main factors: payment history, amounts owed, length of credit history, new credit, and credit mix
Recognize that payment history is typically the single largest factor in most scoring models
Know that a higher score generally means lower interest rates on loans and credit cards
Check your credit report periodically for errors, since you're often entitled to a free report annually
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Understanding Credit Scores" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What is typically the single biggest factor affecting a credit score?

modules.pro_tip: Check your credit report at least once a year for errors or fraudulent accounts, since these can silently hurt your score.

modules.title: Understanding Credit Card Interest and Fees

steps: Recognize that debit cards spend money you already have, with no debt risk

learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Understanding Pay Stubs and Deductions

steps: Identify gross pay at the top, the total earned before any deductions

modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Understanding Pay Stubs and Deductions" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: If gross pay and net pay differ significantly, what commonly accounts for the difference?

modules.title: Understanding Index Funds and Diversification
modules.description: Index funds pool money to buy a broad basket of stocks or bonds tracking a market index, offering instant diversification and historically strong long-term returns with lower fees than actively managed funds. This lesson introduces index investing as a beginner-friendly strategy.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Understanding Index Funds and Diversification

Index funds pool money to buy a broad basket of stocks or bonds tracking a market index, offering instant diversification and historically strong long-term returns with lower fees than actively managed funds.
steps: Understand diversification: spreading investments across many companies reduces the risk of any single one failing
Learn that an index fund automatically buys many companies, such as all those in a major stock market index
Compare expense ratios, since index funds typically have much lower fees than actively managed funds

modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Understanding Index Funds and Diversification" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why does buying an index fund reduce risk compared to buying a single company's stock?
quiz.a: It spreads money across many companies at once, so the poor performance of any one company has a much smaller impact overall

modules.pro_tip: Look for low expense ratios when choosing an index fund, since fees compound over time and quietly eat into long-term returns.

modules.title: Understanding Loans and Interest Rates
modules.description: Loans allow borrowing a lump sum to be repaid over time with interest, and understanding how interest rates affect total repayment cost is essential before taking on any debt. This lesson covers loan terms, APR, and total cost of borrowing.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Understanding Loans and Interest Rates
Loans allow borrowing a lump sum to be repaid over time with interest, and understanding how interest rates affect total repayment cost is essential before taking on any debt.
steps: Understand principal is the original amount borrowed, separate from interest charged

modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Understanding Loans and Interest Rates" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why can a loan with a lower monthly payment sometimes end up costing more overall?

modules.pro_tip: Always calculate the total repayment cost of a loan, not just the monthly payment, before deciding it's affordable.

modules.title: Avoiding and Escaping Predatory Lending

modules.title: Negotiating Salary and Compensation

Lifestyle inflation happens when spending rises to match increased income, preventing meaningful progress toward savings and financial goals even as earnings grow.
steps: Recognize lifestyle inflation: automatically upgrading spending every time income rises
When receiving a raise, direct a portion automatically to savings or investments before adjusting spending
Distinguish between meaningful quality-of-life upgrades and mindless spending increases
Revisit financial goals regularly to ensure spending still aligns with priorities
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Avoiding Lifestyle Inflation" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What is a practical strategy to prevent lifestyle inflation after a raise?
quiz.a: Automatically directing a portion of the raise to savings or investments before it becomes part of regular spending habits

modules.pro_tip: When you get a raise, increase your savings rate by half the raise amount and only let the other half increase spending.

modules.title: Understanding Contracts and Financial Agreements

steps: Read the entire contract before signing, including any fine print or footnotes
Identify the term length and any penalties for early cancellation or breaking the agreement
Look for automatic renewal clauses that could extend the contract without active consent

modules.title: Protecting Yourself from Financial Fraud and Scams

modules.title: Understanding Identity Theft Protection
modules.description: Identity theft occurs when someone uses your personal information without permission, often to open accounts or make purchases in your name, and prevention and quick response both matter. This lesson covers protective habits and recovery steps.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Understanding Identity Theft Protection
Identity theft occurs when someone uses your personal information without permission, often to open accounts or make purchases in your name, and prevention and quick response both matter.
steps: Shred documents containing sensitive information like account numbers before discarding them
Use strong, unique passwords and enable two-factor authentication on financial accounts
Check credit reports regularly for unfamiliar accounts or inquiries
If identity theft occurs, report it immediately to your bank, credit bureaus, and relevant authorities
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Understanding Identity Theft Protection" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What is a simple habit that helps prevent identity theft from discarded mail or documents?
quiz.a: Shredding documents that contain account numbers or personal information before throwing them away

modules.pro_tip: Freeze your credit with the major credit bureaus if you suspect identity theft, which blocks new accounts from being opened in your name.

modules.title: Comparing Renting vs. Buying a Home
modules.description: Deciding whether to rent or buy a home depends on factors like how long you plan to stay, upfront costs, and local market conditions, not a one-size-fits-all answer. This lesson teaches a framework for evaluating the decision.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Comparing Renting vs. Buying a Home
Deciding whether to rent or buy a home depends on factors like how long you plan to stay, upfront costs, and local market conditions, not a one-size-fits-all answer.
steps: Compare the upfront cost of a down payment and closing costs versus a security deposit
Estimate how many years you plan to stay in one place, since buying usually pays off only after several years
Factor in ongoing costs of ownership: maintenance, property tax, and insurance, versus the flexibility of renting
Consider using an online rent-vs-buy calculator with your specific numbers rather than general rules of thumb
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Comparing Renting vs. Buying a Home" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why does the length of time you plan to stay in a home matter for the rent-vs-buy decision?
quiz.a: Buying involves high upfront transaction costs that typically only pay off if you stay long enough to build equity and amortize those costs

modules.pro_tip: Run your specific numbers through a rent-vs-buy calculator rather than relying on generic advice, since local markets vary widely.

modules.title: Planning for Major Life Expenses
modules.description: Major life expenses like a wedding, a car, or a child's education require dedicated, advance planning since they're too large to cover from regular monthly cash flow. This lesson teaches how to plan and save for large predictable future costs.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Planning for Major Life Expenses
Major life expenses like a wedding, a car, or a child's education require dedicated, advance planning since they're too large to cover from regular monthly cash flow.
steps: Estimate the total cost of the upcoming major expense as accurately as possible

materials_needed: Sight savings goal tracker or spreadsheet
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Planning for Major Life Expenses" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why is it helpful to use a separate, dedicated account for a major savings goal like a wedding or car?

modules.pro_tip: Break a large, distant savings goal into a required monthly savings number so it feels concrete and trackable rather than overwhelming.

modules.title: Estate Planning Basics: Wills and Beneficiaries

modules.title: Financial Planning for Freelancers and Gig Workers
modules.description: Freelance and gig income is often irregular and doesn't have automatic tax withholding, requiring different budgeting and tax-saving strategies than traditional employment. This lesson covers key adjustments for non-traditional income.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Financial Planning for Freelancers and Gig Workers
Freelance and gig income is often irregular and doesn't have automatic tax withholding, requiring different budgeting and tax-saving strategies than traditional employment.
steps: Set aside a portion of every payment, often 25-30%, into a separate account for taxes owed

Track business expenses carefully, since many may be tax-deductible

modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Financial Planning for Freelancers and Gig Workers" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why should freelancers set aside money for taxes with every single payment rather than at year end?

modules.pro_tip: Budget off your lowest typical income month, not your best month, since gig and freelance income can vary significantly.

modules.title: Saving for Education with 529 Plans

learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Saving for Education with 529 Plans

modules.description: A personal financial plan ties together budgeting, saving, investing, insurance, and goal-setting into one cohesive strategy for long-term financial health. This capstone lesson guides putting together all previously learned concepts into a single written plan.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Preparing a Personal Financial Plan

steps: Summarize your current financial picture: income, expenses, debts, assets, and net worth

modules.title: Basic Motion Blocks

learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Basic Motion Blocks

modules.title: Costumes and Simple Animation
modules.description: Sprites can have multiple costumes (images), and switching between them rapidly creates the illusion of animation, similar to a flipbook. This lesson teaches how to animate a sprite by cycling through costumes.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Costumes and Simple Animation
Sprites can have multiple costumes (images), and switching between them rapidly creates the illusion of animation, similar to a flipbook.
steps: Open the costumes tab to view all costumes available for a sprite

materials_needed: Scratch project with a sprite that has multiple costumes
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Costumes and Simple Animation" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why is a 'wait' block usually paired with a 'next costume' block when animating?

modules.title: Using the Say and Think Blocks
modules.description: The 'say' and 'think' blocks let sprites display speech and thought bubbles, useful for storytelling, instructions, and giving projects personality. This lesson covers timed and looping dialogue blocks.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Using the Say and Think Blocks
The 'say' and 'think' blocks let sprites display speech and thought bubbles, useful for storytelling, instructions, and giving projects personality.
steps: Drag a 'say Hello! for 2 seconds' block and click it to see the speech bubble appear and disappear
Use a plain 'say' block without a duration to make a bubble that stays until changed
Use 'think' blocks similarly to show a character's thoughts instead of speech
Chain multiple say blocks in sequence to create a short conversation
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Using the Say and Think Blocks" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What is the difference between 'say for 2 seconds' and just 'say'?
quiz.a: 'Say for 2 seconds' automatically clears the bubble after 2 seconds; plain 'say' keeps the bubble showing until another block changes or clears it

modules.pro_tip: Chain a sequence of 'say' blocks to build a simple back-and-forth conversation between characters.

modules.title: Basic Sound Effects and Music
modules.description: Scratch includes a sound library and lets you record custom sounds, adding audio feedback and music that make projects feel alive. This lesson covers adding, playing, and timing sound blocks.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Basic Sound Effects and Music
Scratch includes a sound library and lets you record custom sounds, adding audio feedback and music that make projects feel alive.
steps: Open the sounds tab and choose a sound from the built-in library or record a new one

learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Simple Repeat Loops

modules.title: If-Else for Two-Way Decisions

The 'if-then-else' block extends basic conditions by running one set of blocks when a condition is true and a different set when it's false, covering both outcomes in a single block.
steps: Drag an 'if then else' block into the code area

modules.title: Introduction to Variables
modules.description: Variables are named containers that store changing information, like a score or a player's name, and are fundamental to almost every interactive Scratch project. This lesson covers creating and using a simple variable.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Introduction to Variables
Variables are named containers that store changing information, like a score or a player's name, and are fundamental to almost every interactive Scratch project.
steps: Click 'Make a Variable' in the Variables category and give it a clear name
Use a 'set variable to' block to assign it an initial value
Use a 'change variable by' block to increase or decrease its value during the project
Check the variable's checkbox to display its current value on the stage
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Introduction to Variables" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What is the difference between 'set' and 'change' blocks for a variable?
quiz.a: 'Set' assigns an exact new value, overwriting whatever was there before; 'change' adds or subtracts an amount from the current value

modules.pro_tip: Give variables clear, descriptive names, like 'score' or 'lives', rather than vague names like 'var1', to keep scripts readable.

modules.title: Building a Simple Score Counter
modules.description: Combining variables with events and conditions creates a working score system, a common feature in Scratch games. This lesson walks through building a click-based score counter from start to finish.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Building a Simple Score Counter
Combining variables with events and conditions creates a working score system, a common feature in Scratch games.
steps: Create a variable named 'score' and set it to 0 when the green flag is clicked
Add a 'when this sprite clicked' event block to the same sprite
Inside that event, add a 'change score by 1' block
Run the project and click the sprite repeatedly to watch the score variable increase
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Building a Simple Score Counter" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

modules.title: Building Custom Blocks (My Blocks)

learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Building Custom Blocks (My Blocks)

steps: Click 'Make a Block' in the My Blocks category and give it a descriptive name

modules.title: Introduction to Lists (Arrays)
modules.description: Lists store multiple pieces of data together, like a collection of high scores or player names, unlike a single variable which holds only one value at a time. This lesson introduces creating and using a basic list.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Introduction to Lists (Arrays)
Lists store multiple pieces of data together, like a collection of high scores or player names, unlike a single variable which holds only one value at a time.
steps: Click 'Make a List' in the Variables category and give it a name
Use 'add [item] to list' to insert new items into the list
Use 'item # of list' to retrieve a specific item by its position number

modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Introduction to Lists (Arrays)" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: How is a list different from a regular variable?

modules.pro_tip: Use 'delete all of list' at the start of a project if you want to clear old data before adding new items each session.

modules.title: Cloning Sprites for Repeated Objects
modules.description: Cloning creates temporary copies of a sprite at runtime, essential for games needing many similar objects like bullets, enemies, or falling items, without manually duplicating sprites. This lesson introduces the clone system.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Cloning Sprites for Repeated Objects
Cloning creates temporary copies of a sprite at runtime, essential for games needing many similar objects like bullets, enemies, or falling items, without manually duplicating sprites.
steps: Add a 'create clone of myself' block to generate a new clone when triggered
Add a 'when I start as a clone' hat block on the same sprite to define clone behavior
Use 'delete this clone' within that script to remove clones when they're no longer needed, like leaving the screen
Test by triggering clone creation repeatedly and observing multiple copies behaving independently
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Cloning Sprites for Repeated Objects" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why is it important to delete clones once they're no longer needed?
quiz.a: Clones that are never deleted keep accumulating and consuming memory and processing power, which can slow down or crash the project

modules.pro_tip: Always pair 'create clone of myself' with a corresponding 'delete this clone' condition, such as leaving the screen, to avoid clone buildup.

modules.title: Detecting Collisions Between Sprites
modules.description: Collision detection, checking whether two sprites are touching, is central to most Scratch games, from catching falling objects to avoiding obstacles. This lesson covers using the 'touching' sensing block effectively.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Detecting Collisions Between Sprites
Collision detection, checking whether two sprites are touching, is central to most Scratch games, from catching falling objects to avoiding obstacles.
steps: Use a 'touching [sprite]' block inside an 'if then' condition to detect collision
Combine it with a 'forever' loop so the game continuously checks for collisions
Trigger a response when a collision is detected, such as changing score or playing a sound
Test the collision at different sprite sizes and positions to confirm it works reliably
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Detecting Collisions Between Sprites" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why is a collision-check often placed inside a 'forever' loop rather than checked just once?
quiz.a: Sprite positions change constantly during a game, so collisions need to be checked continuously, not just at a single moment

modules.pro_tip: Combine 'touching' checks with 'if then' inside a forever loop as the standard pattern for real-time collision detection in games.

modules.title: Using the Pen Extension to Draw
modules.description: The Pen extension lets sprites draw trails as they move, useful for creating drawing tools, spirograph patterns, or visualizing motion paths. This lesson introduces the pen down, pen up, and pen color blocks.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Using the Pen Extension to Draw
The Pen extension lets sprites draw trails as they move, useful for creating drawing tools, spirograph patterns, or visualizing motion paths.
steps: Add the Pen extension from the extensions library at the bottom left

modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Using the Pen Extension to Draw" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What is the difference between 'pen down' and 'pen up'?

modules.title: Sensing Blocks: Distance, Mouse, and Timer
modules.description: Sensing blocks let a project detect real-time information like distance to a point, mouse position, or elapsed time, expanding what a project can react to. This lesson covers several key sensing blocks beyond simple touching checks.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Sensing Blocks: Distance, Mouse, and Timer
Sensing blocks let a project detect real-time information like distance to a point, mouse position, or elapsed time, expanding what a project can react to.
steps: Use 'distance to [mouse-pointer]' to measure how far a sprite is from the cursor
Use 'mouse x' and 'mouse y' to track the cursor's exact position
Use the 'timer' block combined with 'reset timer' to measure elapsed time in a project
Combine these sensing values with conditions to build interactive, time-based, or proximity-based behavior
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Sensing Blocks: Distance, Mouse, and Timer" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: How can the 'timer' block be used to build a simple countdown or time-based challenge?

modules.pro_tip: Reset the timer explicitly at the start of a level or game using 'reset timer', since it otherwise keeps counting from when Scratch was opened.

modules.title: Building a Simple Chase Game
modules.description: A chase game, where one sprite tries to catch or avoid another, combines movement, sensing, and collision detection into a complete simple game. This lesson walks through building the full mechanic step by step.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Building a Simple Chase Game
A chase game, where one sprite tries to catch or avoid another, combines movement, sensing, and collision detection into a complete simple game.
steps: Set up one sprite to be controlled by arrow keys using a forever loop and key-press checks
Set up a second sprite to move randomly or toward the player using 'point towards' and 'move steps'
Add a collision check using 'touching' inside a forever loop on either sprite

modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Building a Simple Chase Game" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: What combination of blocks is needed to make an enemy sprite chase the player automatically?
quiz.a: A forever loop combined with a 'point towards [player]' block and a 'move steps' block, so the enemy continuously reorients and moves toward the player

modules.pro_tip: Use 'point towards' before 'move steps' inside a forever loop as the standard pattern for one sprite chasing another.

modules.title: Multiple Costumes for Game States

learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Multiple Costumes for Game States
Switching costumes based on game logic, not just for animation, lets a single sprite visually represent different states, like a character being 'normal' versus 'hurt'.
steps: Create or import multiple costumes representing different states of the same sprite
Use 'switch costume to' combined with an if-condition to change appearance based on game logic

materials_needed: Scratch project with a multi-costume sprite
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Multiple Costumes for Game States" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

modules.title: Creating a Simple Platformer Mechanic (Gravity and Jumping)
modules.description: Simulating gravity and jumping in Scratch involves continuously changing a sprite's y-position downward unless it's on the ground, then briefly reversing that with a jump input. This lesson introduces basic platformer physics logic.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Creating a Simple Platformer Mechanic (Gravity and Jumping)
Simulating gravity and jumping in Scratch involves continuously changing a sprite's y-position downward unless it's on the ground, then briefly reversing that with a jump input.
steps: Create a variable for vertical speed and continuously subtract from it inside a forever loop to simulate gravity
Add a condition checking if the sprite is touching the ground to stop it from falling further
Detect a jump key press and, only if touching the ground, set vertical speed to a positive upward value
Apply the vertical speed to the sprite's y-position each loop cycle to create smooth jumping motion
materials_needed: Scratch project with a player sprite
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Creating a Simple Platformer Mechanic (Gravity and Jumping)" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why is a jump input usually only allowed when the sprite is 'touching the ground'?
quiz.a: Without that check, players could jump repeatedly in mid-air, breaking the intended physics of the game

modules.pro_tip: Use a dedicated variable for vertical speed rather than directly changing y each frame, since it makes gravity and jumping feel much smoother.

learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Building a Simple Quiz Game

steps: Use 'ask [question] and wait' to prompt the player for an answer, storing it in the 'answer' variable

modules.title: Creating a Local Two-Player Game
modules.description: Local multiplayer games let two players use different sets of keys on the same keyboard to control separate sprites simultaneously, adding a social, competitive dimension to Scratch projects. This lesson covers structuring controls for two independent players.

steps: Assign one set of keys, like arrow keys, to control the first player sprite

modules.title: Using Variables for Multiple Lives
modules.description: A 'lives' system extends a score-like variable to track how many chances a player has left before the game ends, a common mechanic requiring careful decrement and game-over logic. This lesson builds a working lives system.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Using Variables for Multiple Lives
A 'lives' system extends a score-like variable to track how many chances a player has left before the game ends, a common mechanic requiring careful decrement and game-over logic.
steps: Create a 'lives' variable and set it to a starting value, like 3, when the green flag is clicked

quiz.q: What condition should typically trigger the 'game over' logic in a lives-based game?

modules.title: Building a Simple Scrolling Background
modules.description: Scrolling backgrounds create the illusion of movement across a larger world by continuously shifting a background sprite, a common technique in racing or side-scrolling games. This lesson covers the wrap-around scrolling technique.
learning_objectives: Understand and safely practice: Building a Simple Scrolling Background
Scrolling backgrounds create the illusion of movement across a larger world by continuously shifting a background sprite, a common technique in racing or side-scrolling games.
steps: Use a background sprite wider than the stage itself
Continuously decrease its x-position inside a forever loop to create leftward scrolling motion
Check if the background has scrolled completely off-screen, and reset its x-position to create a seamless loop
Adjust scroll speed by changing how much the x-position changes each loop cycle
materials_needed: Scratch project with a background sprite (wider than the stage)
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Building a Simple Scrolling Background" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: How is a seamless, endless scrolling background typically achieved with a single or paired sprite?

modules.pro_tip: Use two copies of the same background positioned side by side, resetting whichever one scrolls fully off-screen, for perfectly seamless scrolling.

Debugging is the systematic process of finding why a program isn't behaving as expected, an essential skill as projects grow more complex.
steps: Click individual blocks in isolation to test whether they behave as expected on their own
Use the variable checkbox display to watch values change in real time as the script runs
Add temporary 'say' blocks to display variable values or confirm a script section is being reached
Break a large script into smaller pieces and test each piece separately to isolate the problem
materials_needed: Scratch project with an intentional bug to fix
modules.hands_on_activity: Practice "Debugging: Finding and Fixing Script Errors" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed.

quiz.q: Why is clicking individual blocks in isolation a useful debugging technique in Scratch?
quiz.a: It narrows down exactly which specific block or section is causing unexpected behavior, rather than guessing across a large script

modules.lesson_text:
Debugging: Finding and Fixing Script Errors is a skill worth learning properly rather than casually. Debugging is the systematic process of finding why a program isn't behaving as expected, an essential skill as projects grow more complex. This lesson introduces common Scratch debugging strategies. This lesson walks through the skill from first principles: what it is, why it matters, what you need before you begin, how to work through it step by step, the mistakes that most commonly trip up beginners, and how to practise it until it becomes reliable under real conditions rather than something you can only do on a good day.

Before touching the steps, it helps to understand why this skill earns a place in the curriculum. Skills like this one compound: each hour of correct, focused practice makes the next hour more productive, and the habits you build here -- preparing properly, working in the right order, checking your results -- transfer directly to every other skill in this pathway. Learners who rush past the fundamentals usually have to come back and relearn them later, at greater cost. Taking the time to get the basic pattern right the first time is the single most efficient thing you can do.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to: Understand and safely practice: Debugging: Finding and Fixing Script Errors; Debugging is the systematic process of finding why a program isn't behaving as expected, an essential skill as projects grow more complex. Keep these objectives visible as you work -- they are the measuring stick for whether the practice is working, and each one is phrased as something you can actually demonstrate rather than something you vaguely feel familiar with. Vague familiarity is the great impostor of learning; demonstrable ability is the real thing.

Preparation comes first. For this lesson you will want: Scratch project with an intentional bug to fix. Lay everything out before you start rather than fetching things mid-task; interruptions are where beginners lose focus and where avoidable mistakes creep in. Check the condition of what you are using -- worn, damaged, or makeshift equipment makes every step harder and can make some steps unsafe. If you are missing something, it is almost always better to postpone the practice session than to improvise with a poor substitute while you are still learning what 'correct' feels like.

Now work through the core sequence. Take each step slowly the first several times; speed comes later, and comes faster if you don't chase it early. Step 1: Click individual blocks in isolation to test whether they behave as expected on their own. Once this feels comfortable, try to notice what changed compared with your first attempt; that awareness is itself a skill and accelerates everything that follows. Step 2: Use the variable checkbox display to watch values change in real time as the script runs. Do this deliberately and check the result before moving on -- each step in the sequence assumes the previous one was done correctly. Step 3: Add temporary 'say' blocks to display variable values or confirm a script section is being reached. If this step feels awkward at first, that is normal; repeat it in isolation a few times until it smooths out before continuing. Step 4: Break a large script into smaller pieces and test each piece separately to isolate the problem. Pay particular attention here, because this is a step where small errors tend to compound later in the sequence.

Beginners tend to make the same handful of mistakes with skills like this, and knowing them in advance helps you catch them early. The first is rushing: performing the motions of the steps without the attention that makes them stick, which produces the appearance of practice without the benefit. The second is skipping preparation, which quietly raises the difficulty of everything downstream. The third is practising errors -- repeating a step incorrectly until the wrong version becomes the habit, which then takes far longer to unlearn than it would have taken to learn correctly. If you notice any of these patterns in yourself, stop, slow down, and rebuild the step from its correct form.

Keep the safety guidance in mind throughout: Temporarily display a variable's value on stage or with a 'say' block; seeing the actual value often reveals the bug immediately. This is not boilerplate -- the caution exists because the risk it names is the one most often realised when people are careless with this material. Good practitioners are not the ones who never think about risk; they are the ones who manage it so habitually that it looks effortless.

For practice, start here: Practice "Debugging: Finding and Fixing Script Errors" slowly and safely, focusing on correct form before speed. Treat that as a template you can repeat and extend. A useful structure is short, frequent sessions -- fifteen to twenty focused minutes several times a week will outperform a single long weekend session, because skills consolidate between practices, not just during them. Keep a simple log of what you practised and what felt difficult; over a few weeks the log becomes a map of your progress and tells you exactly what to work on next.

Check your understanding before moving on. Consider this question: Why is clicking individual blocks in isolation a useful debugging technique in Scratch? The answer -- It narrows down exactly which specific block or section is causing unexpected behavior, rather than guessing across a large script -- is worth actually reasoning through rather than just reading, because the reasoning is what you will rely on when a real situation doesn't look exactly like the practice one.

Once the basic sequence is reliable, progress it deliberately. First add consistency: can you perform the skill correctly five times in a row? Then add mild pressure: time constraints, an observer, or slightly less ideal conditions. Then add variation: change the context enough that you must adapt rather than replay a memorised script. This staged progression -- reliability, pressure, variation -- is how training programmes in everything from medicine to sport build skills that hold up in the real world, and it applies just as well here.

Remember where this sits in the wider Coding with Scratch pathway: the lessons before it built the context this one relies on, and the lessons after it will assume the ability you are building now. If any prerequisite feels shaky, a quick review before the next session is cheap insurance.

Finally, connect this lesson to the bigger picture. No single skill stands alone: this one links naturally to its neighbours in the pathway, and fluency here will make several later lessons noticeably easier.
